question: Should default `openclaw doctor --lint` omit legacy state, session transcript/snapshot, and skills readiness checks while exposing `defaultEnabled` as the public opt-out field for core and plugin health checks?
rationale: Code and tests can prove the selector mechanics, but they cannot decide the desired default diagnostic noise, existing automation compatibility, or permanent plugin-health contract shape.

options.title: Accept the narrower default profile
options.body: Keep these checks explicit-only by default and land after maintainer review acknowledges the upgrade and plugin-contract impact.

options.title: Keep selected checks in default lint
options.body: Restore any check family maintainers still want in default `doctor --lint`, then update the audit table and docs accordingly.

options.title: Pause the public SDK field
options.body: Keep the internal selection behavior for core checks but defer plugin-facing `defaultEnabled` until the SDK contract is separately approved.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrower default profile
recommendation.body: Keep these checks explicit-only by default and land after maintainer review acknowledges the upgrade and plugin-contract impact.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame ties this owner to the lint selector and registry surface that defines the default profile behavior.
